description: Hardware/material library, seeded with the NAS1351/NAS1352 socket head cap screw catalog (25 entries, geometry computed per ASME B1.1). Seven of the original 32 were removed: #5-44, #5-40, 9/16-18 and 9/16-12 because neither standard lists them (both skip dash 05 and dash 9, so they could not be procured to the spec they named), and #1-64, #3-48, #3-56 as sizes this programme does not use plus the NASM21042 (8 sizes) and NAS1291 (12 sizes, A286 CRES only) self-locking nut catalogs. The DABJ course book Section 9 validation fixture that used to live here as a temporary 33rd bolt entry, two extra "(DABJ)"-suffixed materials, and one boltSpec has been REMOVED and moved inline into validation.dabjSection9 (see that function's header), so the answer key no longer depends on library content. JSON has no comments; each entry's 'source' field records free-text provenance: DABJ-cited values vs standard handbook fills vs transcribed spec-sheet values. Each entry's 'origin' field ('baseline' or 'custom'; absent = 'baseline') is the separate baseline-protection flag: save() writes only custom entries and load() re-merges this shipped baseline (see data.Library). THREAD FORM RESOLVED 2026-07-29: NAS1351/NAS1352 specify UNRF/UNF (UNRF-3A on procurement drawings), not UNJ, so the ASME B1.1 UN stress areas used here are correct. DABJ Appendix B assumes UNJF and its rated loads therefore imply a ~8% larger At -- do NOT pair DABJ's rated loads with these UNRF entries. See VALIDATION.md, 'UN vs UNJ thread form'. NUTS ADDED 2026-07-30: NASM21042 and NAS1291 both specify true UNJ threads (UNJC/UNJF) for their nut sizes -- this is a DIFFERENT thread form from the NAS1351/NAS1352 bolt catalog above; nut entries carry the UNJC/UNJF designator in their 'thread' field for this reason. NASM21042 carries an ESSENTIAL USAGE ADVISORY (safety-of-flight restriction per NASM33588 / NASA-STD-5020B Appendix B.4.2.1d) recorded on every NASM21042 entry's 'source'. NAS1291 Rev 16 struck out all steel variants; only A286 CRES (450 F finish, key suffix M) is seeded. WASHERS ADDED 2026-07-30: NAS620 'WASHER, FLAT, REDUCED OUTSIDE DIAMETER' (16 sizes, #0-1/4, Reduced OD) and NAS1149 'WASHER, FLAT' (42 sizes, #0-3/4, Standard OD) are now a MANAGED section like nuts (washer(), washersFor(), washerSpecs(), addWasher(), washerKeys(), duplicateAsCustom); washers are geometry only (innerDiameter/outerDiameter/thickness), no rated loads. Each key is the bare document-number+size-code form with no material/finish letters (NAS620-<sizeCode> for plain steel per that standard's own hyphenated bare form; NAS1149<size-and-thickness-code> with no hyphen, matching that standard's no-separator part-number assembly) -- material is chosen separately in the GUI's washer-material dropdown, never carried in the key. DELIBERATE OMISSION: NAS1149 Table I also lists NO.9, NO.11, NO.12 and sizes .875-2.500; none are seeded because the bolt catalog stops at 3/4 with no #9/#11/#12, so they could never be resolved by washersFor(). INSERTS ADDED 2026-08-03: 30 NASM33537 helical-coil tapped-hole geometry entries (Stanley HELI-COIL catalogue HC2000 Rev 12 Table VII p.20, identical to NASM33537 Rev 4 Table IV), covering every NAS1351/NAS1352 size except #0-80 and #5-44, for which no helical insert is offered in either document. These carry TAPPED-HOLE GEOMETRY ONLY -- no strength data exists to seed, because the catalogue defers to Technical Bulletin 68-2 and 68-2 publishes charts rather than tables. Keys are synthetic (see any entry's source). The section is now a MANAGED section like nuts and washers (insert(), insertFor(), addInsert(), insertKeys(), duplicateAsCustom); insertFor() takes no spec argument (only one insert spec, NASM33537, is seeded, so a family filter would be unused).

bolts.source: NAS1351 socket head cap screw (UNF). Thread geometry computed per ASME B1.1 UN thread formulas: minor dia = D - 1.299038P, pitch dia E = D - 0.649519P, At = (pi/4)*((E + minor)/2)^2. THREAD FORM RESOLVED 2026-07-29: NAS1351/NAS1352 specify UNRF/UNF (procurement drawings call UNRF-3A), NOT UNJ. UNR mandates a rounded external-thread root but keeps UN basic major/pitch/minor diameters, so the UN stress area applies and these values are correct. (UNJ per MIL-S-8879 has an enlarged controlled root radius and a ~8% larger At; DABJ Appendix B assumes UNJF, which is why its design tables and rated loads imply At = 0.0951 for 3/8 rather than 0.0878.) Head bearing dia = SHCS head OD (tabulated for numbered sizes); full shank, bodyDiameter = nominal. No threadLength: thread length is a per-part (length-dependent) property.
